articles.title: Millrace Overflows its Banks
articles.deck: Three days of rain send the river over Mill Road and into the low end of Tannery Street. Residents move cars and sandbag doors.
body: The Millrace rose over its banks Monday morning, and by noon water was running across Mill Road at the footbridge and into the low end of Tannerv St. Fire crews from the Eastgate company went door to door on Tannery and Foundry streets asking families to leave by the Lower Millrace road if they could.

The river crested Tuesday at 14 feet, more than four feet above the old 1972 mark, the worst flood on the Millrace since then. Water came up through basement drains and into at least thirty homes. Several garages on the south end of Tannery St. took water to the rafters of their doors. Public works crews worked through the night on the sandbag line behind the mill, which held in most places.
“We have never seen it come up this fast,” said Stanley Wojcik, who has lived at the corner of Tannery and Mill for 22 years. “The water was in the kitchen before I got my boots on.”

The Red Cross opened a shelter at St. Brendan’s hall, and by Wednesday afternoon some 60 people had signed in. County officials say damage assessments will begin next week. More coverage, including the south end of Tannery Street, is on pages 3 and 4.
